\[ \eqalign{ \int_{-\infty}^0 \dfrac {\textrm{d}z}{\sqrt{1-z}} & = \lim_{a \to -\infty} \int_{a}^0 \dfrac {\textrm{d}z}{\sqrt{1-z}}\\[5pt] & = \lim_{a \to -\infty} \left[-2\sqrt{1-z} \right]_{a}^0 \\[5pt] &=-2\cdot\lim_{a \to -\infty}\left(\sqrt{1-0}-\sqrt{1-a} \right)\\[5pt] &=-2+2\cdot\lim_{a \to -\infty}\sqrt{1-a}\\[5pt] &= -2+2\cdot\infty\\[5pt] &=\infty. } \]

Therefore, the integral is divergent.

We proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

\begin{align*} \displaystyle \int_1^\infty \dfrac{1}{2-3z} \,\textrm{d}z &=\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \int_1^a \dfrac{1}{2-3z} \,\textrm{d}z\\[5pt] &=\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[ -\dfrac13 \cdot \ln|2-3z| \right]_1^a\\[5pt] &= -\dfrac13 \cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \big[ \ln|2-3z| \big]_1^a\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac13 \cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left( \ln|2-3a| -\ln|-1| \right)\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac13 \cdot \lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left( \ln|2-3a| \right)\\[5pt] &=-\dfrac13 \cdot \left( \infty \right)\\[5pt] &=-\infty. \end{align*} Therefore, the integral is divergent.

First, we substitute $u=z+2.$ Differentiating, we get

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}z} = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u =\textrm{d}z. \]

Since $u \to \infty$ when $z \to \infty,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=z+2$ is as follows:

$z$ $-1$ $\infty$
$u$ $1$ $\infty$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

\[ \int_{-1}^\infty \dfrac{6}{(z+2)^4} \,\textrm{d}z = \int_1^\infty \dfrac{6}{u^4} \,\textrm{d}u \]

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

\begin{align*} \displaystyle \int_{-1}^\infty \dfrac{6}{(z+2)^4} \,\textrm{d}z &=\int_1^{\infty} \dfrac{6}{u^4} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=6\int_1^{\infty} u^{-4} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=6\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \int_1^a u^{-4} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=6\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[-\dfrac1 3u^{-3}\right]_1^a \\[5pt] &=-2 \cdot \lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[\dfrac{1}{u^{3} } \right]_1^a \\[5pt] &=-2\cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[\dfrac{1}{a^{3} } -\dfrac{1}{1^{ 3} } \right]\\[5pt] &=-2\cdot \left( 0-1 \right)\\[5pt] &=2. \end{align*}

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
First, we substitute $u=x+1.$ Differentiating, we get

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x} = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u =\textrm{d}x. \]

Since $u \to \infty$ when $x \to \infty,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=x+1$ is as follows:

$x$ $0$ $\infty$
$u$ $1$ $\infty$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

\[ \int_0^\infty \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)^9}} \,\textrm{d}x = \int_1^\infty \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u^9}} \,\textrm{d}u \]

Finally, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to\infty.$

\begin{align*} \displaystyle \int_0^\infty \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(x+1)^9}} \,\textrm{d}x &=\int_1^{\infty} \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{u^9}} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=\int_1^{\infty} u^{-{9}/{2}} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \int_1^a u^{-{9}/{2}} \,\textrm{d}u \\[5pt] &=\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[-\dfrac2 7 u^{-{7}/{2}}\right]_1^a \\[5pt] &=-\dfrac2 7 \cdot \lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[u^{-{7}/{2}}\right]_1^a \\[5pt] &=-\frac{2}{7}\cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow\infty} \left[\dfrac{1}{a^{7/2}} -\dfrac{1}{1^{7/2}} \right]\\[5pt] &=-\frac{2}{7}\cdot\left(0-1\right)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{2}{7}}. \end{align*}

question.text: Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
We proceed by setting the lower bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to-\infty.$

\begin{align*} \int_{-\infty}^{-1} \dfrac{35}{x^8} \,\textrm{d}x & =35\lim_{a\rightarrow-\infty} \int_a^{-1} x^{-8} \,\textrm{d}x\\[5pt] &=35\lim_{a\rightarrow-\infty} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{7}x^{-7} \right]_a^{-1}\\[5pt] &=-5\cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow-\infty} \left[ \dfrac{1}{x^7} \right]_a^{-1}\\[5pt] &=-5\cdot\lim_{a\rightarrow-\infty} \left[ \dfrac{1}{(-1)^7}- \dfrac{1}{a^7} \right]\\[5pt] &=-5\cdot\left(-1-0\right)\\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{5}. \end{align*}
